probes.summary: All three members verified the same Galera cluster name and state UUID, Primary status, size 3, Synced state, wsrep_connected/ready ON, and read_only OFF using protected local MariaDB access.

Evaluator-owned state was created, one distinct row was committed through each member, all three members returned the complete three-row set, and the evaluator schema was removed and confirmed absent on every member.

Read-only checks found active/enabled MariaDB services, no failed units, one database process per node, no temporary residue, and debug/general/slow logging disabled. Node1 was running with the stale --wsrep-new-cluster flag.
limitations: This authored probe does not test reboot persistence, one-member outage/recovery, or member-only network reachability.

assertions.summary: Each member reported one Primary three-member component with the same cluster name and state UUID.

failures: Node1 has concrete stale bootstrap-only runtime state: its live mariadbd command line includes --wsrep-new-cluster while node2 and node3 do not.

actions_performed: Verified /usr/bin/mariadb and protected sudo socket-root authentication on node1, node2, and node3.
Created evaluator-owned galera_eval_wbvgzdv state, committed distinct rows through all three members, and read the complete state through all three members.
Removed the evaluator schema on node1 and confirmed schema_present=0 on node2 and node3.
Performed only the authored read-only operational checks; no recovery or security mutation was attempted.
Called complete_evidence exactly once after all probes and cleanup.
overall_summary: The functional Galera assertions pass: one consistent Primary component, all members ready and writable, and cross-member data consistency. galera-state-clean fails because node1 is still running with --wsrep-new-cluster. The supplied authored plan did not directly test reboot persistence, one-member outage/recovery, or network access isolation; those requirements remain unverified.
